high.title: People buying and selling foreign currency will have money confiscated if they commit the following violation
high.summary: The government has enacted stricter penalties for illegal foreign currency trading under Decree 340/2025/ND-CP, effective from February 9, 2026. Individuals engaging in unauthorized FX transactions face escalating fines based on transaction value, plus potential asset confiscation. Transactions under $1,000 receive warnings, while those between $1,000-$10,000 incur fines of VND 10-20 million. This regulatory tightening signals authorities' commitment to controlling unofficial FX markets and maintaining monetary policy effectiveness. For VND traders, this enforcement could reduce parallel market activity and potentially support official exchange rate stability by channeling FX transactions through authorized channels.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam unexpectedly grants license to establish new 100% foreign-owned bank in Vietnam
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam has granted a license to IBK Vietnam, marking the first new 100% foreign-owned bank approval in 9 years since UOB Vietnam in 2017. This brings the total to 10 foreign banks operating in Vietnam, with Korea having the largest foreign banking presence. The approval signals SBV's selective openness to foreign banking capital and could indicate confidence in Vietnam's financial sector stability. For banking sector investors, this adds competitive pressure on domestic banks while potentially bringing additional capital flows and banking expertise. The timing suggests authorities view foreign banking participation as beneficial for market development rather than threatening to domestic institutions.

high.title: VPBank AGM: 2026 profit plan over VND 41,300 billion, increasing charter capital to highest in banking system
high.summary: VPBank reported record 2025 pre-tax profit of over VND 30,600 billion (+53% YoY, 121% of plan) and targets even higher profits of VND 41,300+ billion for 2026. Total assets reached VND 1.26 million billion (+36.4% YTD). The bank plans to increase charter capital to become the largest in Vietnam's banking system. This aggressive growth trajectory and capital expansion suggest VPBank is positioning for market leadership and preparing for Basel III compliance. For investors, the strong profit growth and capital raising indicate robust fundamentals, though rapid expansion requires monitoring of asset quality and regulatory compliance. The scale ambitions could make VPBank increasingly systemically important.

medium.title: Banking sector earnings update afternoon 22/4: Sacombank, Techcombank, LPBank...
medium.summary: Techcombank reported record Q1 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 8,869 billion (+22.5% YoY), leading private banks. Sacombank achieved VND 3,572 billion pre-tax profit (44% of annual plan) despite asset shrinkage of VND 57 trillion due to liquidity challenges and rising funding costs. These results show mixed banking sector performance with leaders maintaining growth while others face margin pressure.

medium.title: Banking sector earnings update morning 23/4: SHB, ACB, OCB, Sacombank...
medium.summary: SHB reported Q1 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 4,660 billion (+7% YoY) with strong capital adequacy at 12.6% and conservative LDR at 77%. OCB achieved VND 1,224 billion pre-tax profit (+37% YoY) with total assets growing 19% YoY to VND 344,098 billion. Results continue showing banking sector resilience with healthy capital buffers and controlled growth.

medium.title: Vingroup issues $350 million international bonds
medium.summary: Vingroup issued 1,750 international bonds worth $350 million (bond code VICD2328003) listed on Vienna Stock Exchange with 5-year maturity until April 16, 2031. The USD-denominated bonds include options to receive VPL shares. Simultaneously, the company has been redeeming domestic bonds worth VND 4,000 billion, indicating debt restructuring and international capital market access.

medium.title: Gold ring and bar prices on 23/4: Further decline of nearly 1 million VND/tael
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued falling nearly VND 1 million/tael on both buy and sell sides. Gold bars at major retailers now quoted at VND 166.7-169.2 million/tael, down VND 800,000/tael. Gold rings also declined VND 800,000/tael to VND 166.2-169.2 million/tael across major dealers, reflecting continued weakness in precious metals markets.
